findings.evidence: The cmdk list keeps an invalid combobox/listbox structure. Command.List is given aria-label="Commands" (line 99), but cmdk's List reads its `label` prop and hard-sets aria-label on the rendered div, so the listbox is actually named "Suggestions". Each Command.Item uses asChild (line 107) around a native <button role="button"> (lines 109-111); Radix Primitive/Slot lets the child's role win, so cmdk's role="option" is lost. A jsdom render of the palette (scratch probe) produced: <input role="combobox" aria-label="Search commands" aria-labelledby="radix-:r1:"> and <div role="listbox" aria-label="Suggestions"> containing <button type="button" role="button" aria-selected="true"> rows. The input also carries both aria-label and aria-labelledby, so its accessible name is the hidden "Command palette" text, not "Search commands".
findings.description: The packaged palette exposes an invalid combobox/listbox: a listbox whose children are role="button" (not role="option") with aria-selected (unsupported on a button), a list announced as "Suggestions" instead of the intended "Commands", and a search input named "Command palette" instead of "Search commands". Screen-reader and assistive-technology users cannot reliably discover the commands or hear which one is active, which fails USR-006 section 5.8 (support assistive technologies) and its accessibility requirement. Pass `label="Commands"` to Command.List instead of aria-label, and keep cmdk's option role on the items (e.g. drop the child role="button" so the slot's role="option" applies, or render cmdk's default element), then update the A1 role assertions that expect buttons.

verifications.evidence: Palette: CommandPalette.tsx:45-54 now records document.activeElement on mount and restores it in the unmount cleanup (after both Escape at line 62 and choose at line 78), skipping the page body and disconnected/hidden elements, and falling back to the always-visible footer button[aria-label="Toggle sidebar"]. src/features/command-palette/CommandPalette.test.tsx:111-120 mounts the palette from a focused opener, presses Escape and asserts the opener has focus; it passes. Git drawer: App.tsx:241-245 records the opener in openGitTab, and closeGitTab (App.tsx:246-255) restores it (falling back to the Show/Hide git tools chip) instead of leaving focus on the hidden Close button; src/App.layout.test.tsx:158-174 clicks Changes, closes the drawer and asserts the Changes control regains focus while the Close button does not. The full suite passes (44 files, 432 tests).
